question: Should OpenClaw add `hostIntegrationBundle` as a permanent core plugin-manifest and registry contract, or should host-specific composition remain outside the core manifest?
rationale: The linked implementation introduces a new external plugin manifest surface with durable versioning and ownership semantics; source-level review cannot determine the intended public contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Confirm the field name, stable versioning and duplicate-ownership rules, then review the linked implementation as the proposed core API.

options.title: Keep composition plugin-owned
options.body: Decline the new core manifest surface and direct host plugins to retain composition metadata in their own package or service boundary.

options.title: Request a smaller generic seam
options.body: Define the minimum manifest or registry abstraction needed before accepting any host-bundle-specific data model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the field name, stable versioning and duplicate-ownership rules, then review the linked implementation as the proposed core API.

likelyOwner.reason: The related manifest-first plugin-inventory work makes this the strongest available routing candidate, though direct current-main ownership evidence is limited.
